setlist.title: It Must Have Been The Roses

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Let It Grow** (3 reviews): Hornsby's keyboard playing added a lot to this song; Reviewer judged this version good [24][25][26]
- **It Must Have Been The Roses** (2 reviews): Reviewer found this nice, one of the show's better moments despite a generally weak show; Reviewer always enjoys hearing this song and singles it out [25][26]
- **Hell In A Bucket** (1 review): Weir kept fiddling with his rack, walked offstage with a roadie and adjusted knobs while the song played [18]
- **Cold Rain & Snow** (1 review): Hornsby played accordion here, though the reviewer wished he had played piano [24]
- **Foolish Heart** (1 review): Runs over nineteen minutes into space and is singled out as pretty nice [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1991-04-09.fob.schoepsCMC34.unknown.GEMS.93471.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 20 songs; 181 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd91-04-09.sbd.miller.25466.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 174 min; rated 2.7/5 by 10 [2]. Said about its sound: Sound problems affected the start of the show and held the band back through nearly all of set one [20]
- **gd1991-04-09.154481.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac16**: soundboard; 18 songs; 175 min [3]
- **gd1991-04-09.152233.ultramatrix.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 18 songs; 178 min [4]
- **gd1991-04-09.154480.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac16**: soundboard; 18 songs; 178 min [5]
- **gd91-04-09.sbd.ingle.10061.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 15 songs; 141 min; rated 4/5 by 3 [15]

## Around the show

- It was the final night of the spring tour, and the reviewer thought the band seemed tired [20]
- Vendors lined the street in unprecedented numbers; on day two, mounted police, DEA helicopters and undercover agents appeared [21]
- A Deadhead drowned in a nearby lake during the run [21]
- Last show of the spring tour; the band scheduled two Orlando shows but played three [22]
- The day was beautiful and tickets seemed fairly plentiful, with the run extended to a third show [23]
- A man swam out into the lake around which fans parked and drowned, bringing heavy police presence [23]
- Reviewer found it a recap of the whole tour rather than a distinct performance, and a letdown [18]
- Show again closed with Throwing Stones into Not Fade Away, followed by a Brokedown Palace encore, as on earlier nights [21]
- At the time the second set felt somewhat recycled compared with other shows [23]
- The other two Orlando nights were better, notably for Rubin and Cherise on April 7 [24]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1991-04-09.fob.schoepsCMC34.unknown.GEMS.93471.flac16**: transferred by Todd Evans, Jamie Waddell; source: Schoeps CMC34 (ORTF) -> Panasonic sv255 [1]
- **gd91-04-09.sbd.miller.25466.sbeok.shnf**: source: Recording Info: SBD -> Master Dat (Panasonic 3700) -> Master Cassette (Tascam 122mkIII/TDK SA-X100) Transfer Info: Master Cassette (Nakamichi CR-7A) -> Dat… [2]. Also: Cassette played on Nakamichi CR-7A to Sony R500 DAT, edited in Samplitude, and converted to SHN by Charlie Miller [2]
- **gd1991-04-09.154481.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  April 10, 2021; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [3]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; this upgrades an earlier version that ran almost two percent fast; Several masters were combined to make the show complete [3]
- **gd1991-04-09.152233.ultramatrix.miller.flac2496**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  April 9, 2021; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [4]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; several masters were used to complete the show [4]
- **gd1991-04-09.154480.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  April 9, 2021; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [5]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; several masters were used to complete the show; This is a 16-bit/44.1k downconversion of the 24-bit/96k release [5]
- **gd91-04-09.sbd.ingle.10061.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>??>DAT>??>CDR (Liberated Bootleg) [15]. Also: Complete show was submitted for circulation, sourced from the cassette master of the soundboard [17]
